episode.subject: British soldier lichen
episode.title: The unfinished argument
episode.body:
A boot pressed the far end of our plank. The crack beneath us opened.

I stopped arguing with my green partner and waited for the wood to settle.

When the foot lifted, he asked what I'd been about to say. I couldn't remember. He said he could, but it could wait.

proposals.visualReview: Exact frame individually opened. Central upright red-tipped lichen and flanking structures are sharp against pale weathered wood; deep split directly below its base is visible. Background soft focus leaves the subject distinct. Four further exact observation frames opened separately, including split-plank context and whole overgrown trailer. Wider frame corroborates old wooden truckbed description, but no boot is present.
proposals.fictionBoundary: The existing split wood and attached lichen are observed. Boot contact, crack widening, movement and the exchange between principal voices are invented. Neither the still nor observer records the incident. No claim of fungal eating of its substrate, separation of symbiotic partners, locomotion, truck operation or documented injury. The wider trailer is overgrown and decayed; a moving-truck premise was rejected.
proposals.continuity: Retains established one-speaking-lichen/two-principal-voices embodiment, without asserting exactly two biological organisms. Fiction stays in northern Georgia mixed woodland34.68/-84.08; observer source is Thurman, New York. A weathered abandoned wooden truckbed at the woodland edge is a proposed local substrate detail, not relocation to the real observation. No new identity, avatar or autonomous red-cap individuals.
proposals.proseReview: An external disturbance interrupts their habitual argument. The green partner remembers the argument but chooses to postpone it after their shared alarm. No pronoun dispute or explained moral. Root must judge whether the brief change in their relationship earns a Story and whether visible split wood sufficiently supports the invented pressure incident.
